summary: 60-minute customer success/check-in focused on contract extension mechanics, adding EU capacity and tightening latency SLOs. Emerald is evaluating a blended model (hosted + dedicated reserved capacity for peak traffic) and asked for a billing amendment to reflect staged bursts. Security and data residency were discussed; Emerald emphasized SOC 2 and KMS integrations. Redwood committed to benchmarking and a revised quote.
topics: Capacity uplift and staged burst pricing
Contract amendment wording and billing cadence
transcript:
00:00:04 Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we have about an hour. Quick roll call?
00:00:12 Dana (Emerald): Hi Dana here.
00:00:14 Omar (Emerald): Omar on the call.
00:00:16 Sophie (Emerald): Sophie for procurement.
00:00:18 Carlos (Redwood SE): Carlos from Redwood, SE.
00:00:21 Maya: Great. Goal for today is to align on the renewal amendment, the EU capacity add, and the latency SLA ask Dana raised. We also want to surface any open security questions.
00:00:36 Dana: Yes, thanks. To recap — we've been happy with the overall throughput but we've seen spikes where our latency at p95 drifts above 400ms and that impacts user workflows. We're considering a committed dedicated pool to stabilize those spikes.
00:00:49 Carlos: Right, and to be explicit, dedicated capacity gives you predictable queuing and affinity for KV cache locality, so p95 should tighten. The trade is cost — dedicated headroom vs. pay-as-you-go.
00:01:02 Dana: Understood — Sophie, do you want to say where procurement stands on the billing amendment?
00:01:06 Sophie: We're okay in principle but need the billing cadence and a clear definition of burst units. We don't want surprise egress or hidden token charges during peak runs.
00:01:16 Maya: Totally, we'll put that in the amended SOW and pricing appendix. Proposal: blended model — baseline hosted at committed monthly units, reserved dedicated pool for peaks with an agreed burst bucket and per-burst rate. We'll quantify burst tiers in the quote.
00:01:30 Omar: Two technical asks: one, can Redwood guarantee p95 under a coldstart storm scenario? We run large inter-day batch jobs that cause spikes. Two, network topology — we need VPC peering and static egress IPs for our firewall rules.
00:01:44 Carlos: For coldstart we can do a warmup policy and pre-warmed containers; that reduces coldstart penalties. We'll show results from a warm-concurrency test. For VPC we support VPC peering and dedicated private deployments; static IPs are possible for egress through NAT gateways in a private deployment.
00:02:01 Dana: What about KMS and key custody? We need customer-managed keys for PII in EU instances.
00:02:06 Maya: We support KMS integration and HSM-backed key stores in the Private offering. We'll attach the KMS checklist and your security contact can work with our security team.
00:02:15 Marcus (Emerald Security): Marcus here — clarify SOC 2 version and how audit logs map to our retention policy.
00:02:20 Anita (Redwood CSM): We can share the SOC 2 report and a mapping doc. Audit logs are configurable for retention and can be exported to your SIEM. We'll include retention SLAs in the amendment.
00:02:33 Dana: Timeline: we really need this in place for the first week of Sept, which means contract signed by end of July ideally. Can Redwood hit that?
00:02:42 Maya: That's doable if we get the decision and the VPC/network info in the next two weeks. We'll prioritize the quote and the benchmark results.
00:02:51 Sophie: One caveat: procurement needs a clear cancellation and termination for convenience clause if usage drops below threshold after six months.
00:02:58 Maya: We'll put in a churn protection clause and a 30/60/90 review cadence in the amendment.
00:03:05 Carlos: Back to performance — can we get a sample of Emerald's production traces? If you provide a two-week log of request rates and sequence length distribution we can replay on a dedicated pool and report p95/p99.
00:03:17 Omar: Yes, we can share anonymized traces. We'll also share the KV cache hit rates.
00:03:25 Maya: Great. Action items recap coming at the end.
00:03:28 Dana: One more — we've been running some lateral comparisons with Anthropic and VendorX on cost per 1M tokens. Are you able to show TCO for our workload?
00:03:37 Maya: We can produce a TCO comparison — we'll include token price, expected cache savings, and amortized reserved costs. The Optimize toolkit can model your workload and show break-even for dedicated vs hosted.
00:03:49 Carlos: Also we'll include quantization options — if you accept a small quality delta, some quantized variants reduce GPU footprint and cost per token.
00:03:58 Dana: Noted.
00:04:01 (15:11) Maya: Okay, let's jump into specifics on the billing amendment draft — I have three models on the slide: baseline hosted + reserved burst; 2) committed dedicated with overage; 3) hybrid with auto-fallback to a lower-cost variant.
00:04:17 Sophie: I like the hybrid but procurement needs the math. The worst-case cost exposure needs to be explicit.
00:04:23 Maya: We'll make a worst-case workbook and an expected-case workbook. We'll share as a Google sheet link after the call.
00:04:31 Carlos: Technical note — for EU residency we recommend deploying the dedicated pool in eu-west-1 and pinning workload routing. That gives lowest latency for EU users.
00:04:40 Omar: How long to spin the dedicated pool up if we commit?
00:04:44 Carlos: Typically 72 hours for provision + warmup depending on capacity; for urgent onboarding we can expedite if contract is signed and hardware is available.
00:04:53 Dana: So final Qs: SLA for latency — can we get a p95 SLA at 200ms?
00:04:59 Carlos: 200ms p95 is aggressive for some LLM footprints at production sequence lengths. We can do p95=200ms for smaller models or quantized variants; for large models p95=250-300ms is more realistic on Dedicated with warm KV cache. We should benchmark with your traces.
00:05:16 Dana: Okay we accept benchmarking as the decision gate.
00:05:19 Maya: Perfect. We'll run benchmarks, provide the workbook, and an amended SOW with billing table and SLA language.
00:05:26 Sophie: Procurement will need sample contract language for termination, data residency, and billing net-30.
00:05:32 Maya: We'll include those.
00:05:35 Marcus: Security will onboard with Redwood's security team next week — preferred time 2pm GMT Tuesday.
00:05:41 Anita: I'll set that up.
00:05:43 Maya: Great. Any other questions?
00:05:46 Dana: Nothing else. Thanks.
00:05:48 Maya: Thanks everyone — recap in chat and email with links.
00:05:52 (62:00) END OF TRANSCRIPT
